title: California Eviction Defense (Unlawful Detainer)
description: Step-by-step guide for tenants facing eviction in California. Covers the full unlawful detainer process from notice receipt through post-judgment options.

steps.title: Receive and review the eviction notice
steps.description: Carefully read every word of the notice. The type of notice determines your response window and available defenses. Common types: 3-Day Pay or Quit, 3-Day Cure or Quit, 30-Day or 60-Day No-Fault Notice.
actions: Identify the notice type (Pay or Quit, Cure or Quit, No-Fault, Terminate Tenancy)
Verify the notice is properly served (personal service, substituted service, or posting + mail)
Count your response days carefully — start counting the day AFTER service
Check that the landlord's name, property address, and amounts owed (if any) are accurate
Photograph the notice and envelope immediately

deadlines.notes: 3-day notices count calendar days including weekends. If day 3 falls on a weekend or court holiday, deadline extends to next business day.

steps.title: Evaluate your options and defenses
steps.description: Before the landlord can file in court, you have options. If you have a Pay or Quit notice, paying all rent owed stops the eviction. If you have a Cure or Quit, fixing the lease violation stops it. Evaluate whether any defenses apply.
actions: If Pay or Quit: calculate exact amount owed and determine ability to pay
If Cure or Quit: identify the lease violation and whether you can fix it
Identify potential defenses: improper notice, landlord retaliation, landlord failure to maintain habitable conditions, rent was paid, wrong amount on notice
Check if local rent control or just-cause eviction ordinances apply (LA, SF, Oakland, etc.)
Contact a local tenant legal aid organization for a free case evaluation

deadlines.notes: You must act before the notice period expires or the landlord may file in court.

steps.agency: Local tenant legal aid (Bay Area Legal Aid, Inner City Law Center, etc.)

steps.title: Pay rent or cure the violation
steps.description: If you can pay the full amount owed or fix the violation within the notice period, the eviction stops. Get written proof of payment.
actions: Pay the full amount stated in the notice (partial payment does NOT stop the eviction)
Pay by cashier's check or money order — keep your receipt
Demand a written receipt from the landlord
If landlord refuses payment, document the refusal in writing (this is a defense)
Keep copies of all payment records permanently

steps.title: Prepare for court if not paying or landlord files anyway
steps.description: If you cannot pay, do not cure, or the landlord files an Unlawful Detainer lawsuit regardless, you must prepare your court response.
actions: Gather all evidence: lease, payment records, repair request letters, communications
Document any habitability issues with photographs and dated notes
Contact legal aid immediately — many offer emergency assistance for eviction cases
Identify witnesses who can testify on your behalf
Begin preparing your Answer to the UD complaint

deadlines.notes: After being served with the UD Summons and Complaint, you have 5 business days to file your Answer with the court.

steps.title: File your Answer with the court
steps.description: You must file a written Answer (Form UD-105) with the Superior Court within 5 business days of being served the UD complaint. Filing an Answer preserves your right to a hearing.
actions: Complete Form UD-105 (Answer — Unlawful Detainer) — available at court self-help centers
Check all applicable affirmative defenses on the form
Make 3 copies: original for court, one for you, one to serve on landlord's attorney
File at the court clerk's office and pay the filing fee (or request fee waiver Form FW-001)
Serve a copy on the plaintiff (landlord's attorney) by mail or personal delivery
File Proof of Service (Form POS-030) with the court

deadlines.notes: Day 1 is the day AFTER you were personally served. Deadline is strictly enforced — default judgment can be entered if you miss it.

steps.title: Attend the court hearing
steps.description: After you file your Answer, the court will schedule a trial, usually within 20 days. Prepare thoroughly. Bring all evidence.
actions: Confirm hearing date, time, and courtroom from your court notice
Organize evidence in a binder: lease, rent receipts, repair requests, photos, communications
Prepare a written timeline of events
Subpoena witnesses if needed (ask self-help center for assistance)
Arrive 30 minutes early — dress professionally
Present your defenses clearly and calmly; address the judge as 'Your Honor'
Request a continuance if you need more time to prepare (not guaranteed)

deadlines.notes: Trial is typically set within 20 calendar days of the Answer being filed.

steps.title: Receive judgment and evaluate next steps
steps.description: The judge will issue a judgment. If you win, you stay. If you lose, you have options before a lockout occurs.
actions: If you WIN: obtain certified copy of judgment for your records
If you LOSE: you typically have 5 days before the landlord can get a Writ of Possession
If you LOSE: consider filing a Notice of Appeal (must be within 30 days of judgment)
If you LOSE: negotiate a move-out agreement with landlord to avoid formal lockout
If you LOSE: request a stay of execution from the court if you need more time
Document everything that happens after the judgment

deadlines.notes: Sheriff cannot execute lockout until at least 5 days after judgment. Appeal deadline is 30 days.

steps.title: Handle lockout or move-out
steps.description: If the landlord obtains a Writ of Possession, the Sheriff will post a 5-day notice to vacate. Know your rights during this process.
actions: Remove all belongings before the Sheriff returns — abandoned property rules apply
Document the condition of the unit with video and photos on move-out
Request an itemised accounting of your security deposit within 21 days
File a claim in Small Claims Court if security deposit is wrongfully withheld
Check if the eviction affects your rental history — some credit reporting protections apply
Seek emergency housing assistance through 211.org or local social services

deadlines.notes: Landlord must return security deposit or itemized deductions within 21 days of move-out.
